_readme: Factors we could not source yet. Every entry is our own estimate, in hundredths (100 = 1.00), with a deliberately wide low/high so the range widens when it is used. To replace one with a sourced figure, add the source under data/factors/sources/, derive it in src/lib/factor-derivation.ts, and delete the entry here. See data/factors/README.md.

under-1.label: Licensed under 1 year (age 26 and up)
under-1.why: No survey we found prices a driver licensed under a year. It should cost at least as much as 1–3 years, so we use the 1–3 year factor and widen the top by a fifth.

two-or-more.label: Two or more at-fault accidents
two-or-more.why: Two North Carolina 3-point accidents would total 6 points; the NC page does not list the surcharge for 6 points, so we added two single-accident surcharges (1 + 0.70 + 0.70). The low end is one accident; the high end is the largest surcharge on the NC table (12 points, +340%).

yes.label: Good-student discount (under 26)
yes.why: Many insurers offer a discount for a B average or better.

yes.label: Driver-training discount (under 22)
yes.why: Many insurers offer a discount for completing driver education.

250-500-250.label: Higher limits (250/500/250)
250-500-250.why: Higher limits cost more for the liability part of the premium.

500.label: $500 deductible
500.why: A lower deductible raises the collision and comprehensive part of the premium.

2000.label: $2,000 deductible
2000.why: A higher deductible lowers the collision and comprehensive part of the premium.

yes.label: Loan or lease (gap coverage)
yes.why: Lenders usually require collision and comprehensive, and many drivers add gap coverage.

4-7.label: Vehicle 4–7 years old
4-7.why: Older cars are worth less, so collision and comprehensive cost less.

8-12.label: Vehicle 8–12 years old
8-12.why: Older cars are worth less, so collision and comprehensive cost less.

13-plus.label: Vehicle 13 or more years old
13-plus.why: Older cars are worth less, so collision and comprehensive cost less.

liability.label: Share of a full-coverage premium that is liability
liability.why: The value comes from ISO loss costs; the low/high around it is our estimate of how much the split varies by driver, car, and state.

vehicle-model.label: How closely a company's price follows HLDI losses for a model
vehicle-model.why: Insurers rate vehicles with their own symbols. Those follow loss experience, but not exactly.

vehicle-model-years.label: Model year outside HLDI's years
vehicle-model-years.why: HLDI's results are for 2022–24 models; an older or newer design may differ.

trim-limited.label: Car version only partly matched
trim-limited.why: We are not sure which version of the car it is.

trim-unresolved.label: Car version not found
trim-unresolved.why: We could not find which version of the car it is.

state-unknown.label: Moving to a state without a typical price
state-unknown.why: Average prices differ a lot between states.

state-typical.label: Moving between states with typical prices
state-typical.why: A state's typical price moves differently for different drivers.
